s1.syndrome_frame: Postpartum headache with worsening course and associated symptoms
salient_findings: Layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection on noncontrast CT
key_facts: 31 days postpartum after elective cesarean delivery
Initial mild global headache 8 days postoperatively
Normal prothrombin time, partial prothrombin time, and international normalized ratio
Noncontrast CT showed extra-axial collection with areas of linear and crescentic hyperdensity

raw.syndrome_frame: Postpartum headache with worsening course and associated symptoms
salient_findings: Layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection on noncontrast CT
key_facts: 31 days postpartum after elective cesarean delivery
Initial mild global headache 8 days postoperatively
Normal prothrombin time, partial prothrombin time, and international normalized ratio
Noncontrast CT showed extra-axial collection with areas of linear and crescentic hyperdensity

differentials: Cerebral vasculitis due to systemic lupus erythematosus
Intracranial hemorrhage due to arteriovenous malformation
Cerebral venous thrombosis due to protein S deficiency
Dural sinus thrombosis with hemorrhagic transformation
Intracranial hemorrhage due to cocaine use
Intracranial dural sinus thrombosis due to factor V Leiden mutation

Intracranial hemorrhage due to arteriovenous malformation
Cerebral venous thrombosis due to protein S deficiency
Dural sinus thrombosis with hemorrhagic transformation
Intracranial hemorrhage due to cocaine use
Intracranial dural sinus thrombosis due to factor V Leiden mutation

shortlist.label: Subdural hematoma
shortlist.why_kept: Noncontrast CT showed extra-axial collection with areas of linear and crescentic hyperdensity, consistent with subdural hematoma

shortlist.label: Spontaneous intracranial hypotension
shortlist.why_kept: Postpartum headache with worsening course, potentially related to spinal anesthesia and subsequent CSF leak

shortlist.label: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Severe headache, nausea, and malaise, with normal vital signs and no meningeal signs, consistent with posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome

shortlist.label: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Headache with worsening course, with areas of linear and crescentic hyperdensity on CT, potentially indicating cerebral venous sinus thrombosis

shortlist.label: Chronic subdural hematoma
shortlist.why_kept: Initial mild headache 8 days postoperatively, with subsequent worsening, potentially indicating chronic subdural hematoma

raw.rationale: The patient's worsening headache over 3 days, severe nonpositional headache, and the noncontrast CT showing a layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection are consistent with a chronic subdural hematoma, which can develop after a traumatic event such as a cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia.

rejected.label: Subdural hematoma
rejected.why: While possible, the term 'subdural hematoma' is more general and does not specify the chronic nature of the condition, which is suggested by the timeline of symptoms.

rejected.label: Spontaneous intracranial hypotension
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with postural headaches that improve with recumbency, which does not match the patient's nonpositional headache.

rejected.label: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by hypertension, seizures, and specific MRI findings, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis
rejected.why: This condition would likely present with more severe and sudden symptoms, and the CT findings do not suggest thrombosis.
